title: U.S. House · Florida's 13th District
area: West-central Florida, including parts of Pinellas County around St. Petersburg and Clearwater.

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Anna Paulina Luna advanced unopposed. Leela Gray won the Democratic primary with 65.1% of the vote against Brandt Robinson and John Liccione.

candidates.name: Anna Paulina Luna

summary.text: Anna Paulina Luna is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 13th Congressional District. An Air Force veteran, she worked in conservative advocacy and media, ran unsuccessfully for Congress in 2020, and won the seat in 2022; she was re-elected in 2024 and is seeking a third term.

background.text: Born in Orange, California in 1989; according to her congressional office, she was raised by a single mother in Southern California.
Served in the U.S. Air Force from 2009 to 2018.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of West Florida in 2017; her congressional biography says the degree is in biology.

Worked as an entrepreneur, director of Hispanic engagement for Turning Point USA, chairwoman of Hispanic initiative for PragerU, and a podcast host with Gingrich 360, and is a published author with Posthill Press.
Ran for Congress in Florida's 13th District in 2020 as the Republican nominee and lost the general election to incumbent Charlie Crist.

Won the 2022 general election for Florida's 13th District, defeating Eric Lynn and other candidates, and took office in January 2023; her office says she is the first Mexican-American woman elected to Congress from Florida.
Serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and chairs the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets.
Her congressional biography says she was named one of Time's next 100 most influential people in 2023 and lives in St. Petersburg with her husband, Andy.

priorities.text: Immigration: says she will fight to finish the border wall, end DACA, restore the Remain in Mexico policy, and oppose amnesty as a pathway to citizenship.
priorities.quote: Anna will fight to finish the border wall, end DACA, restore President Trump’s Remain in Mexico policy, and crack down on criminal illegals in America.

priorities.text: Education: says she will work to expand school choice, ensure parental rights, and protect women's sports.
priorities.quote: Anna will work to advance efforts to expand school choice, ensure parents rights, protect women’s sports, and increase civic literacy.

priorities.text: Government accountability: says she will support a ban on members of Congress and staff becoming lobbyists after leaving office and push to enact term limits for elected officials.
priorities.quote: She will support any ban on Congress or its employees becoming lobbyists to cash out after leaving office. She will also work to enact term limits for elected officials.

summary.text: Leela Gray is the Democratic nominee in Florida's 13th Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army Brigadier General with 30 years of service, she is also a lawyer; she won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 65.1% of the vote. She is running on affordability, government ethics, and support for veterans and seniors.

background.text: Says her family relied on food stamps growing up and that she worked two jobs to pay for college.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Elon University, a graduate degree from the U.S. Army War College, and a law degree from the Stetson University College of Law.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1988 to 2018, rising to the rank of Brigadier General.

According to an EMILYs List endorsement release, her Army career included commanding troops, a peacekeeping mission, and two combat deployments, and after active duty she worked at the State Department as a strategic advisor to U.S. Army Cyber Command.
The same release describes her as a longtime Tampa Bay resident who has mentored entrepreneurs and advocated for veterans.
Defeated Brandt Robinson and John Liccione in the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for Florida's 13th District.

priorities.text: Affordability: says she would push to lower housing-insurance and healthcare costs and provide tax relief to middle-class families and small businesses rather than "the ultra-wealthy and big corporations."
Government ethics: says she would push to ban insider stock trading by members of Congress, enact term limits, and impose a lifetime lobbying ban on former members.
Veterans and seniors: says she would cut red tape at the VA and work to protect and strengthen Social Security and Medicare.

positions.summary: Says Congress must protect and strengthen Social Security and Medicare so seniors "can age with dignity."
Lists ending what she calls "illegal tariffs" among her priorities for reducing costs for families and small businesses.

candidates.name: Tony D'Arrigo

summary.text: Tony D'Arrigo is running with no party affiliation for Florida's 13th Congressional District in the November 3, 2026 general election. He is a hospitality business consultant and owner of an entertainment business based in the Tampa area.

background.text: Born in Hackensack, New Jersey, and raised in Brigantine, New Jersey; moved to Tampa, Florida, in 2014.
Earned a high school diploma from Atlantic City High School.
Has worked as a hospitality business management consultant and is the owner and operator of Two Step Entertainment.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia biography page, campaign website, or completed Candidate Connection survey was found for D'Arrigo in the time available.
